hints.title: Check convergence first
hints.body: Find the first term and common ratio. Use the condition for a finite geometric sum to restrict k.

hints.recap: Solve inequalities on their valid domains, then intersect the restrictions.

hints.pause: Solve this inequality on the convergence interval.

hints.title: Use the original possible choices
hints.body: Shade both restrictions on one number line. Count the original integer choices in their overlap.
hints.recap: With equally likely outcomes, probability is the number of favourable outcomes divided by the total number of outcomes.
hints.pitfall: Do not shrink the denominator to just the convergent choices.
hints.pause: Divide that successful count by the number of original choices.

recall.reminder: With equally likely outcomes, probability is the number of favourable outcomes divided by the total number of outcomes.

solution:
The ratio is r=2k7. Convergence requires −72<k<72, so the integer candidates are −3, …, 3. On this domain, S=41−2k7=287−2k, with positive denominator.

Thus S>3 exactly when 28>21−6k, or k>−76. Intersecting gives k=−1, 0, 1, 2, 3: five successful choices.

There are 11 equally likely original choices, including the ones for which the series diverges. The probability is 511. Answer E.
